description: Map the EBNF rule [sign] digit {digit} directly into an if statement, a required digit check, and a while loop.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `recognize_signed(s)` starts with cursor `i = 0` on line 7. Lines 8-9 translate the optional `[ sign ]` EBNF brackets into `if i < len(s) and s[i] in "+-": i += 1`.

Lines 10-12 require at least one `digit`, returning `False` if the string ended or `s[i]` is not a digit. Lines 13-14 translate `{ digit }` repetition braces into `while i < len(s) and s[i].isdigit(): i += 1`. Line 15 returns `i == len(s)` to confirm the entire string was consumed.

Look at how lines 8-15 mirror `[ sign ] digit { digit }` piece by piece. They use `if` for `[ sign ]`, a guard and `i += 1` for `digit`, and `while` for `{ digit }`. Finally, `i == len(s)` rejects trailing characters.

steps.answer: For `"-"`, line 9 advances `i` to `1`. Line 11 returns `False` because `i >= len(s)` (no required digit follows the sign). For `"4-2"`, the `while` loop stops at `'-'` (`i = 1`). Line 15 returns `False` because `i == len(s)` (`1 == 3`) is `False`.
steps.question: When `recognize_signed` runs on `"4-2"` and `"-"` in the test loop on line 21, which line rejects `"-"` and which line rejects `"4-2"`?

steps.description: Lines 21-22 run `recognize_signed` across seven test strings, accepting `'42'`, `'-42'`, `'+7'`, and `'007'` and rejecting `'4-2'`, `'-'`, and `''`.
While testing `'-'`, line 9 has already consumed `'-'` (`i = 1`). Thus, `i >= len(s)` is `True` on line 10 and line 11 returns `False`.

title: Translating EBNF Into a Hand-Rolled Recognizer
